title: Aging Muscle Has a Hidden Molecular Switch - Nautilus
gist: Aging shifts skeletal muscle from fast-twitch to mitochondria-dependent slow-twitch fibers even as mitochondria decline — a paradox that new research attributes to a hidden molecular switch.

insights.claim: Fast-twitch skeletal muscle fibers rely more on simple carbohydrates and power quick motions like sprinting and jumping, while slow-twitch fibers are packed with mitochondria and serve endurance and posture.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: As people age their bodies shift from fast-twitch to slow-twitch muscle fibers, which is paradoxical because the mitochondria that slow-twitch fibers depend on also lose function with age.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: An unexplained mechanism in sarcopenia is a potential target for longevity and muscle-wasting drug developers.
